# DolphJS

> A TypeScript framework for Node.js. Decorators, dependency injection and validation, on Express or Fastify. This page describes version 3.

Import everything from `@dolphjs/dolph`. Node `^20.19.0 || ^22.13.0 || >=24.11.0`. Each job below has one way to do it, so use that way.

Full docs: https://dolphjs.com/getting-started/

## Project setup

```bash
pnpm install -g @dolphjs/cli
dolph new my-app
dolph generate --all orders   # service, dto, controller, model, specs, component, wired into server.ts
pnpm dev:start
```

`dolph generate` skips files that already exist. `--force` replaces them.

## Where settings go

- Plain values that vary by environment: `dolph_config.yaml`
- Functions and objects: the `DolphFactory` options
- Anything for one route: decorators

## A feature

```ts
// orders.dto.ts
import { IsInt, IsString, Min } from 'class-validator';

export class CreateOrderDto {
    @IsString()
    item: string;

    @IsInt()
    @Min(1)
    quantity: number;
}

// orders.service.ts
import { DService, NotFoundException } from '@dolphjs/dolph';

@DService()
export class OrdersService {
    find(id: string) {
        throw new NotFoundException('order not found');
    }
}

// orders.controller.ts
import { DBody, DParam, Get, Post, Route } from '@dolphjs/dolph';

@Route('orders')
export class OrdersController {
    constructor(private orders: OrdersService) {}

    @Post()
    create(@DBody(CreateOrderDto) dto: CreateOrderDto) {
        return this.orders.create(dto);
    }

    @Get(':id')
    find(@DParam() params: { id: string }) {
        return this.orders.find(params.id);
    }
}

// orders.component.ts
import { Component } from '@dolphjs/dolph';

@Component({ controllers: [OrdersController], services: [OrdersService] })
export class OrdersComponent {}

// server.ts
import { DolphFactory } from '@dolphjs/dolph';

new DolphFactory([OrdersComponent]).start();
```

Routes are prefixed by `routing.base` in `dolph_config.yaml`.

## Responses

- `return` data to send it. It's wrapped as `{ success, status, message, data }`. Strings become `message`.
- `null` sends 204. `undefined` sends nothing, so you can respond yourself.
- `throw` to send an error: `BadRequestException`, `UnauthorizedException`, `ForbiddenException`, `NotFoundException` and so on.
- For another status, take `@DRes() res: DResponse`, call `res.status(201)`, and return as usual.
- HTML only goes out through `res.send()` or `@Render('template')`.

## Parameters

`@DBody(Dto?)`, `@DParam(Dto?)` and `@DQuery(Dto?)` return the whole body, params or query. They take a DTO class, never a field name. With a DTO, invalid input returns 400. Unknown fields are rejected on bodies and params, and dropped on queries.

Also: `@DReq()`, `@DRes()`, `@DNext()`, `@DPayload()`, `@DHeaders()`, `@DCookies()`, `@DAuth()`, `@DFile()`, `@DFiles()`.

## Auth

```ts
const auth = jwtAuth(process.env.JWT_SECRET);

@Shield(auth)                  // every route in the controller
@Route('account')
export class AccountController {
    @Get()
    me(@DPayload() payload: IPayload) {
        return payload;
    }

    @Post('login')
    @UnShield(auth)            // pass the same reference
    login() {}
}
```

- `jwtAuth(secret)` reads `authorization`.
- `jwtAuth(publicKeyPath, { algorithm: 'RS256' })` reads `x-auth-token`.
- `jwtAuth(secret, { cookie: true })` reads the cookie from `newAuthCookie()`.
- `jwtAuth(secret, { authorize: (payload) => boolean })` answers 403 when false.

## Middleware

- Every request: `new DolphFactory([App], { middlewares: [cookieParser()] })`
- One route: `@UseMiddleware(a, b)`, left to right
- `(req: DRequest, res: DResponse, next: DNextFunc)`, and Express middleware works on both adapters
- Async functions on an Express router: wrap in `DolphAsyncMiddleware`

## DolphFactory

```ts
const dolph = new DolphFactory([OrdersComponent], {
    middlewares: [cookieParser()],
    sockets: { component: new ChatComponent(), auth: socketJwtAuth(secret) },
    graphql: { schema, context },   // served at /graphql
    onError: myErrorHandler,        // (err, req, res, next)
    onResponse: myInterceptor,      // (data, req, res) => body
});

await dolph.start();
```

The constructor only stores options. `engine()` wires the server, `ready()` also connects databases, GraphQL and sockets, `start()` also listens, and `stop()` shuts down. `SIGTERM` runs `stop()`. In tests, use `engine()` so nothing connects.

## dolph_config.yaml

```yaml
port: 3300               # PORT in the environment wins
adapter: fastify         # express is the default. fastify needs fastify and @fastify/middie
env: development         # production is the default
jsonLimit: 2mb
routing:
  base: /v1
middlewares:
  helmet: true
  cors:
    activate: true
    origin: https://app.example.com
views:                   # needs all three
  engine: ejs
  dir: views
  assets: public
database:
  mongo:
    url: sensitive       # reads MONGO_URL
    required: false      # start anyway if it can't connect
  typeorm:
    options:
      type: postgres     # any TypeORM driver. Reads SQL_HOST, SQL_USER, SQL_PASSWORD, SQL_URL
      host: sensitive
      username: sensitive
      password: sensitive
      database: my_app
      entities:
        - app/**/*.entity.js
```

A required database that can't connect stops the app at startup.

## Databases

- Mongoose: `@InjectMongo('userModel', UserModel)` on the service, then `userModel!: Model<IUser>`.
- TypeORM: use a getter, because services are built before the DataSource exists:

```ts
private get users() {
    return getDataSource().getRepository(User);
}
```

## Uploads

```ts
@Post('avatar')
@UseMiddleware(auth, imageUpload({ field: 'avatar', maxSize: '2mb' }))
setAvatar(@DFile() image: UploadedImage) {}
```

`imageUpload()` checks real file contents and pixel limits. With `sharp` installed it removes metadata such as GPS, and takes `resize`, `format` and `quality`. For other files use `useFileUploader({ type: 'single', fieldname, extensions, storage })`. Storage is `memoryStorage()`, `diskStorage({ destination })` or `cloudStorage({ put, remove })`.

## Sockets

```ts
@DService()
export class ChatService extends DolphSocketServiceHandler {
    constructor() {
        super();
        this.socket.on('connection', (socket) => {});
    }
}

@Socket({ services: [], socketServices: [ChatService] })
export class ChatComponent extends SocketComponent {}
```

Pass `auth: socketJwtAuth(secret)` in the `sockets` option, or `auth: false` for public sockets. Other origins need `options.cors`.

## Testing

```ts
import { createTestingApp } from '@dolphjs/testing';

const app = await createTestingApp({
    components: [() => import('./orders.component').then((m) => m.OrdersComponent)],
    overrides: [{ service: OrdersService, useValue: mock }],
});

await request(app.engine).get('/v1/orders/1');
await app.close();
```

Pass components as lazy imports, so overrides apply. Add `connect: true` to connect databases.

## Removed in version 3

Don't use these: `SuccessResponse`, `ErrorResponse`, `@JWTAuthVerifyDec`, `@JWTAuthorizeDec`, `@CookieAuthVerifyDec`, `cookieAuthVerify`, `JwtBasicAuth`, `JwtAuthMiddleware`, `validateBodyMiddleware`, `@ValidateReq`, `reqValidatorMiddleware`, `TryCatchAsyncDec`, `TryCatchFn`, `middlewareRegistry`, `dolph.middlewares()`, `enableHelmet()`, `enableCors()`, `setGlobalExceptionHandler()`, `setResponseInterceptor()`, `MVCAdapter`, `autoInitMongo`, `@InjectMySQL`, Sequelize. Base classes such as `DolphServiceHandler` still work, but plain classes are preferred.
